name: The Million Dollar Homepage
title: A Million Pixels, Sold. Now Look at the Dead Links.
claims: Page has a million pixels in a 1000x1000 grid sold at $1 per pixel in 10x10 blocks | 1
Page launched 26 August 2005 | 1
Student sold pixels to raise money for university; was starting a three-year business course; worried about student debt | 1, 2
Brainstorm: wrote "How can I become a millionaire?" and had an answer in twenty minutes | 2
Student said it was a crazy, quirky idea that might work and he had nothing to lose | 2
Priced in US dollars because US had larger online population; pound was about $1.80 and may have made pixels too expensive | 1
Setup cost was €50 (source 1) or about $100 (source 2) | 1, 2
Site was live in about two days | 2
Page had banner, pixel counter, nine-link navigation bar and 10,000 blocks | 1
Smallest purchase was $100; buyers supplied image, link and hover slogan | 1
Promised site would stay up at least five years, until 26 August 2010 | 1
First sale three days after launch, 400 pixels to a friend's music website | 1
After two weeks friends and family had bought 4,700 pixels | 1
Press release sent after the site made $1,000; picked up by the BBC | 1
Press release funded from first sales; story pitched as broke student with quirky way to raise money | 2
The Register ran two articles in September | 1
By end of September $250,000 received; Number 3 on Alexa "Movers and Shakers" behind Britney Spears and Photo District News | 1
Source 2 says $40,000 sold within two weeks; source 1 says 4,700 pixels from friends and family after two weeks | 1, 2
6 October: 65,000 unique visitors and 1465 Diggs; 11 days later 100,000 | 1
26 October: over 500,900 pixels sold to 1,400 customers | 1
New Year's Eve: 25,000 unique visitors per hour, Alexa rank 127, 999,000 pixels sold | 1
1 January 2006: last 1,000 pixels auctioned on eBay to avoid a second page and keep exclusivity | 1
Auction lasted ten days with 99 legitimate bids; bids up to $160,109.99, many retracted or cancelled as hoaxes; he phoned bidders | 1
Winning bid $38,100 from a diet-products online store; he expected higher | 1
Gross total $1,037,100 in five months; expected net $650,000-$700,000 after costs, taxes and charity donation | 1
Spent about $40,000 on maintaining and publicising the site | 2
7 January 2006 email from "The Dark Group" demanded $5,000 by 10 January | 1
Second email demanded $50000, quoted wording; site flooded and crashed | 1
Site inaccessible for a week until host upgraded security with anti-DDoS filtering | 1
He said it was like terrorism and he would not pay | 1
Wiltshire Constabulary's Hi-Tech Crime Unit and FBI investigated; believed to originate in Russia | 1
Auction closed 11 January | 1
Initially uploaded images and links by hand; hired two people | 2
PayPal blocked account; replacement found in three hours; PayPal later re-enabled and both kept | 2
Media in 35 other countries | 2
Week-long US trip with interviews; Richard & Judy; BBC News Magazine profile; Wall Street Journal coverage said celebrity status | 1
Popular Mechanics quote about viral marketing and no content | 1
Nottingham professor called it brilliant in its simplicity | 1
Washington Post writer's "advertising train wreck" and "take a shower" quotes | 1
Copycats appeared almost immediately; hundreds; he said idea only works once and relies on novelty; comedy value | 1
Buyers included casinos, get-rich-quick schemes, dating, loans, free samples, web design, holidays, small businesses | 1
Buyers included producers of a Wal-Mart documentary, Orange, The Times, Independiente Records, Tenacious D, Yahoo! | 1
He dropped out of the degree after one term; later founded companies | 1
He had said he would defer college and had job offers from large internet companies | 2
By 2017 only main page available; sub-pages returned 404 | 1
2017: of 2,816 original links, 547 dead (342,000 pixels, $342,000) and 489 redirected to a different domain (145,000 pixels) | 1
Majority of remaining links do not seem to reflect original purpose | 1
By April 2019 BBC said about 40% of links suffered link rot; still several thousand daily viewers | 1
Alexa rank peaked around 127; 40,044 as of 9 May 2009 | 1
No source states whether anyone was caught for the attack | 1
